rationale: This paper is a pure wastewater-treatment engineering study calibrating a first-order kinetic model of bacterial die-off in a tertiary wastewater storage reservoir used for agricultural and landscape irrigation in Sicily, Italy. It does not examine household or community water or sanitation service access (targeting irrigation instead), contains no legal, administrative, regulatory, or governance mechanism, and measures only microbiological treatment kinetics rather than household service access outcomes.
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both narrow and plain readings of Criterion 2 because the study is purely a technical wastewater-treatment kinetic modelling analysis for agricultural irrigation with no legal, administrative, institutional, or governance component and no household water or sanitation service access outcome.

evidence_quotes.quote: Modelling of bacterial removal in wastewater storage reservoir for irrigation purposes: A case study in Sicily, Italy
The storage results in a tertiary treatment of a continuous inlet flow of activated sludge effluents.
The prediction of the microbiological water quality has been evaluated by means of a non-steady-state first-order kinetic model.
